details.description: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B is a 14-billion-parameter dense reasoning model that DeepSeek created by fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen2.5-14B on roughly 800,000 reasoning traces generated by the full DeepSeek-R1 model, released in January 2025 alongside DeepSeek-R1. It carries R1's step-by-step 'thinking' style of reasoning for math, coding and logic tasks into a mid-sized dense architecture. Fireworks AI serves it with a 131,000-token context length. It is released under the MIT license, while the underlying Qwen2.5-14B base carries an Apache 2.0 license.
advantages: Scores 69.7% pass@1 on AIME 2024, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 93.9% pass@1 on MATH-500, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 59.1% pass@1 on GPQA Diamond, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 53.1% pass@1 on LiveCodeBench, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's model card recommends capping output around 32,768 tokens and notes the model can 'bypass thinking pattern' on some queries, which may reduce answer quality.

DeepSeek's own API changelog labels this reasoning generation 'legacy R1' and discontinued the deepseek-reasoner model id in favor of the DeepSeek-V4 series by July 2026, though the open weights stay available on Hugging Face and via third-party hosts such as Fireworks AI.
use_cases: Complex multi-step reasoning and logic tasks
General text generation with an explicit chain-of-thought 'thinking' step

notes: DeepSeek's model card recommends a maximum generation length of 32,768 tokens for reliable output, well below the 131,072-token max_input/max_output in the catalog facts and the 131,000-token context Fireworks advertises; the catalog's larger figures are kept as authoritative per instructions, but users should know the maker's own tested/recommended length is much shorter. Fireworks lists 14.7B parameters for this checkpoint (Qwen2.5-14B base). The model card's 'outperforms OpenAI-o1-mini across various benchmarks' line is stated only about the sibling DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B; this 14B checkpoint actually trails o1-mini on GPQA Diamond (59.1 vs 60.0) and LiveCodeBench (53.1 vs 53.8), so that advantage was removed rather than misattributed. DeepSeek's own API changelog (api-docs.deepseek.com/updates) shows deepseek-reasoner moved on from DeepSeek-R1 to DeepSeek-V3.1/V3.2-Exp in 2025 and then to the V4 series by mid-2026, referring to this generation as 'legacy R1'.
